PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Gestational Age: 12 weeks (based on ultrasound dating)
Indication for Testing: Prenatal screening for common chromosomal trisomies
Sample Type: Uncultured chorionic villi
Sample ID: [redacted ID]

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on DNA extracted from uncultured chorionic villi using a panel of short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. A minimum of four informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome. Peak area ratios were calculated for all heterozygous markers, with normal diallelic ratios ranging from 0.8-1.4. The presence of three alleles or skewed diallelic ratios (>1.8 or <0.65) would indicate trisomy.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13:
- Markers analyzed: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Result: Normal biallelic pattern observed
- Interpretation: Normal complement for chromosome 13

Chromosome 18:
- Markers analyzed: D18S391, D18S390, D18S535, D18S386
- Result: Normal biallelic pattern observed
- Interpretation: Normal complement for chromosome 18

Chromosome 21:
- Markers analyzed: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1446
- Result: Normal biallelic pattern observed
- Interpretation: Normal complement for chromosome 21

Sex Chromosomes:
- AMELX/Y analysis: XX pattern detected
- Interpretation: Female fetus

OVERALL RESULT: NO ABNORMALITY DETECTED

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis shows a normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) was detected in this sample.

LIMITATIONS
1. This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only
2. Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected by this methodology
3. Structural chromosomal abnormalities, including segmental imbalances, translocations, and microdeletions/duplications are not detected
4. Maternal cell contamination, if present, may mask fetal abnormalities
5. This test does not screen for open neural tube defects or other genetic conditions

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Follow-up cytogenetic analysis (karyotyping) will be performed on cultured chorionic villi to confirm these results and provide a comprehensive chromosomal analysis
2. Results from the cytogenetics laboratory will be reported separately when available
3. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results and any additional testing options
4. Standard prenatal care should continue as recommended by the referring physician

This test was developed and validated by [redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings and other laboratory data.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
CAP Number: [redacted ID] | CLIA Number: [redacted ID]
